title: Model containment via deepest-container semantics, not string-prefix matching
context: Four rounds of code review identified three independent failure modes in absolute-path containment checks: nested worktrees were wrongly attributed to their parent, symlinked aliases weren't recognized, and files literally named '..odd.ts' were mistaken for '..' traversals. All stemmed from string-prefix checks and unresolved path comparison. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Replace naive relative()-startsWith('..') logic with deepestContainer(), which canonicalizes all paths, compares by path-segment boundaries (not string prefixes), finds every worktree containing the absolute file, and selects the most specific (longest-path) match. existsUnder verifies both that containment AND that the file actually exists, preventing any ancestor from swallowing its nested children.
consequences: Nested worktrees (e.g. root/.worktrees/feature) correctly attribute to themselves, not their parent
Worktrees accessed through symlink aliases resolve correctly via canonical path resolution
Files genuinely named '..odd.ts' are no longer mistaken for '..' path traversals
Containment model is now explicit and unit-testable, not implicit in relative-path heuristics
alternatives_rejected: Patching only the string-prefix check (would miss nested/symlink/filename issues and remain fragile)
Checking lexical containment without canonicalizing (would still fail on symlinks and case differences)
Picking any containing worktree instead of deepest (reintroduces nested worktree swallowing)
Avoiding explicit worktree tracking in favor of heuristics (requires re-deriving the container set)
